title: Good Shepherd Dental
subject: Torts
stem:
BARMATRIX Q# 15258_good_shepherd_dental

At Lydia’s private dental office, which she named Good Shepherd Dental Studio, Paul came in for an ordinary paid appointment before a church choir retreat. Lydia, a licensed dentist, was anesthetizing Paul’s jaw before extracting a tooth. Although Lydia used due care, the hypodermic needle broke off in Paul’s gum tissue, causing injury. The needle broke because of a manufacturing defect that Lydia could not have detected.

Is Paul likely to recover damages from Lydia in an action based on strict products liability and malpractice?
call: Is Paul likely to recover damages from Lydia in an action based on strict products liability and malpractice?

choices.B: Yes, based on malpractice, but not on strict products liability.
choices.C: Yes, based on strict products liability, but not on malpractice.

rightExplanation:
A is correct. Paul cannot recover from Lydia on either theory.

Silver Key: When the answers are “neither / malpractice only / products only / both,” treat the choices as a two-switch grid. Test each theory separately, then choose the cell.

Gold Key: Strict products liability targets commercial sellers and distributors, not a professional service provider merely using an instrument during treatment. Lydia used the needle as part of a dental service; she was not selling needles as a product.

Gold Key: Malpractice requires a departure from the professional standard of care. The stem says Lydia used due care and could not detect the defect, so the malpractice switch is also off.

wrongExplanations.B: It gets the products-liability switch right but turns the malpractice switch on. The stem says Lydia used due care. A true version would need facts showing that she departed from the professional standard of care.
wrongExplanations.C: It gets the malpractice switch right but turns the strict-products switch on. Gold Key: a professional who uses a defective instrument while rendering services is not treated as the commercial seller of that instrument.
wrongExplanations.D: It turns both switches on. Silver Key: in a two-theory answer grid, do not answer from injury alone. Test each theory separately. Here both switches are off.

c3.label: Answer array
c3.text:
2×2 theory grid.

* A = no strict products liability / no malpractice.
* B = no strict products liability / yes malpractice.
* C = yes strict products liability / no malpractice.
* D = yes strict products liability / yes malpractice.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: malpractice switch is on even though the stem gives due care.

c3.label: CUT C
c3.text: strict-products switch is on even though Lydia is a dentist rendering a service, not a needle seller.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: both switches are on; it overextends injury + defect into both theories.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text: No two-answer clash remains after the two theory switches are tested.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: Apply the Gold Keys to both switches; choose the “neither” cell.

studentScript: This is a two-switch grid. Product switch: off, because Lydia is a service provider using the needle. Malpractice switch: off, because the stem says due care. Both off means A.

A.signal: The answer is the no/no cell after the two switches are tested.
A.lawyer: Correct. Lydia is not a commercial seller/distributor of needles, and the malpractice theory fails because due care means no departure from the professional standard of care.

B.signal: The answer turns malpractice on despite the due-care fact.
B.lawyer: Incorrect. The products-liability denial is right, but malpractice requires breach of the professional standard of care; the stem supplies due care.

C.signal: The answer uses the manufacturing-defect lure but points strict products liability at a service provider.
C.lawyer: Incorrect. Strict products liability targets commercial sellers/distributors; Lydia used the needle in treatment.

D.signal: The answer converts one injury into recovery on both theories.
D.lawyer: Incorrect. Both theories fail against Lydia: no commercial seller status and no professional-standard breach.

goldKeys.statement: Strict products liability targets commercial sellers and distributors. A professional who merely uses a defective instrument while providing a service is not strictly liable as the product seller.
goldKeys.trigger: Professional treatment + defective instrument + defendant is the treating professional, not the product seller.
goldKeys.unlocks: The manufacturing-defect trap in choices C and D.
goldKeys.authority: Restatement (Second) of Torts § 402A; Restatement (Third) of Torts: Products Liability; Magrine v. Spector.

goldKeys.statement: Malpractice requires a departure from the professional standard of care. Injury during treatment is not enough when the professional used due care.
goldKeys.trigger: The stem says the professional used due care or could not detect the defect.
goldKeys.unlocks: The injury-equals-malpractice trap in choices B and D.

silverKeys.statement: When the choices are neither / theory one only / theory two only / both, do not pick by feel. Test each theory as a separate switch, then choose the matching cell.
silverKeys.trigger: Answer choices split recovery into neither, one theory only, the other theory only, and both.

remediation.title: Two-switch liability grid
remediation.signal: Choices offer neither / one theory / the other theory / both.
remediation.studentMove: Turn each theory on or off independently.
remediation.tinyRule: Do not let one injury automatically satisfy every theory.
remediation.trap: Manufacturing defect plus injury feels like automatic recovery.
